extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, journalists, and general readers interested in ethnic media (primarily U.S.-focused)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize definitions, scope, examples, and evaluative criteria for ethnic media (with emphasis on U.S. scholarship and practice). Includes practical definitions, constituent formats, circulation sectors, and a seven-pronged test for assessing whether an ethnic outlet functions as 'alternative' media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition (Yu Shi)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ethnic media are often regarded as media by and for ethnics in a host country with content in ethnic languages.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shi further notes ethnic media can be published by large ethnic media groups or by small organic ethnic communities; the definition emphasizes orientation toward an ethnic community and language/content directed at that community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner definition (Inga Buchbinder / New America Media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic media is defined as a publication (news, television, radio, online, print, magazine—or any sort of publication) that caters to a specific ethnic community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be in-language or bilingual; scope covers many formats (broadcast, print, online) as long as the outlet targets a specific ethnic community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats and content forms that can constitute ethnic media (John D.H. Downing and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond news and traditional media, ethnic media may include musical culture and forms of religious expression as part of the ethnic media mix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cultural and religious forms, along with language and dialect, can function as media forces providing social/psychic validation between majority and minority groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target circulation sectors (Downing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic media tend to circulate within at least three sectors: indigenous nations and communities, recent migrants, and settled subordinate ethnic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the audience/community loci where ethnic media primarily operate and circulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginalization relative to mainstream media
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic media are often marginalized in mainstream, popular media and are fashioned with a particular ethnic minority group or community in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characteristic (marginalization) is part of how ethnic media are sociologically positioned, relevant to assessing reach, influence, and relationship to dominant media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnic media are not automatically 'alternative media' (case-by-case assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an ethnic media outlet qualifies as alternative media is not definitional by default and must be determined through contextual, case-by-case evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholars and practitioners emphasize the need for discernment and contextual information rather than assuming ethnic = alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yu Shi's seven-pronged test for evaluating an ethnic outlet's 'alternative media' role
rubrics_metrics.description: To evaluate the alternative-media role of an ethnic outlet, reference should be made to: (1) individual place of origin, (2) historical evolution, (3) production process, (4) distribution pattern, (5) ownership, (6) self-identity (non-profit or for-profit; alternative or commercial; or in between), and (7) connection to power groups in local and transnational settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these seven dimensions together to assess whether an ethnic outlet functions as alternative media in its specific context; each prong examines a distinct institutional/contextual aspect (origins, evolution, production/distribution, economic/ownership structure, identity, and power linkages).
